request.title: Review round 1 — requirements baseline REQ-BL-1 (46 requirements)
request.author: masood

threads: "Consecutive samples stay outside the allowed band for 60 s" can be read as 6 or 7 samples at a 10 s sampling period. Say the count, so two testers get the same answer.
Reword SYS-002 to a sample count: 7 consecutive samples (= 60 s at the 10 s sampling period).
The allowed band (2 °C to 8 °C) exists only as a data-dictionary range and in A-04. No requirement states it, so no test can fail if the firmware uses another band.
Add a system requirement that states the allowed band, parent STK-001.
SAF-003 declares a probe fault only outside -40 °C to 60 °C, but ENV-004 says the probe works from -30 °C to 50 °C. A reading of 55 °C is neither a valid reading nor a fault.
Reword SAF-003 to the probe's own operating range, -30 °C to 50 °C.
"Flash" has no rate. A 0.2 Hz blink and a 5 Hz strobe both pass. IEC 60601-1-8 high-priority visual signals flash at 1.4 Hz to 2.8 Hz.
Reword SYS-004 to flash at 2 Hz.
"No valid sample" does not say what valid means. The DS18B20 answers with a CRC; say that a sample with a wrong CRC is not valid.
Reword SYS-012: no sample with a correct CRC for 30 s.
65 dB(A) at 1 m: the test does not say the background noise or the meter. A noisy room makes the test pass or fail by luck.
Rewrite the Verification section: background below 45 dB(A), class 2 meter, on axis at 1 m.
30 s to deliver the log only means something with a full log.
Verification section: run it with 10000 events in the log.

The glossary ends an excursion at the FIRST sample back in the band. A fridge hovering at 8.0 °C would start and end excursions every 10 s — alarm chatter, and a flood of log events. The end needs the same confirmation as the start.
Add a system requirement: excursion end confirmed after 7 consecutive samples inside the band; fix the glossary entry.

After the nurse presses acknowledge the buzzer stops, and nothing ever makes it sound again while the fridge stays warm. IEC 60601-1-8 treats silence as a paused alarm that comes back. Today a single press silences a real excursion for good.
Add a system requirement: the buzzer sounds again 15 min after acknowledge while the excursion continues (15 min is an assumption, A-13).

Every event carries a UTC time stamp, but no requirement says how good the clock must be. An audit trail with a clock that drifts 10 min a week is worthless. (Q-10 asks how it is set; this asks how well it keeps time.)
Add a system requirement on clock drift; Q-10 (how it is set) stays open.
On battery the monitor runs about 4 h and then just stops. Nobody is told before monitoring ends. A silent stop is the worst failure a monitor can have.
Add a safety requirement: buzzer when the battery voltage falls below 3.4 V (EE-REVIEW, A-15).
Read-only access stops a user changing the log, but not a flash bit-flip or a torn write at power loss. Class C audit data needs corruption to be detectable.
Add a system requirement: each log record carries a CRC-32 and a bad record is detected.
What happens at event 10001 is not said. Stop logging? Overwrite the oldest? Either way staff must be warned before history is lost.
Add a system requirement: log-nearly-full warning at 9000 events. The overwrite-or-stop choice goes to the data-retention ADR (Phase 4).
The restart time after a watchdog timeout is given, but not the watchdog timeout itself. A hung task could go unnoticed for minutes.
Noted — the watchdog period is a software-architecture decision (IEC 62304 §5.3); it gets its own ADR and requirement in Phase 7.
"Operate from the internal battery for 4 h" is endurance, a performance property, filed as environmental.
Noted — the kind stays; renaming the id after baseline REQ-BL-1 would break the trace for no gain.
With ±0.5 °C accuracy, a true 8.4 °C can read 7.9 °C: the alarm limit and the accuracy interact. Say whether the band is applied to the reading or with a guard band.
Noted — the band applies to the reading; the residual risk of ±0.5 °C goes into the ISO 14971 hazard analysis in Phase 5 as a named hazard cause.
The power-loss event is logged, but not the power-restore event. An auditor cannot tell how long the fridge ran without mains.
Add a system requirement: log the power restore event with its UTC time stamp.
